title: Abstract ideas
focus: sujog, probhab, shorto, folafol, karon, mulyo, khomota, tatporjo, dik, poristhiti, ghotona, prokriya, mul bishoy, manodondo, subidha, osubidha, gurutto
body:
Abstract nouns are where a home-Bengali speaker usually switches to English: "the main point is...", "it depends on the situation", "what's the purpose". These are the words an educated Kolkata speaker uses for those ideas. They sound natural in serious conversation, not just in writing.

| Romanization | Bengali | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| sujog | সুযোগ | opportunity |
| probhab | প্রভাব | influence, effect |
| shorto | শর্ত | condition, term |
| folafol | ফলাফল | result |
| mulyo | মূল্য | value, worth |
| khomota | ক্ষমতা | power, capability |
| tatporjo | তাৎপর্য | significance |
| dik | দিক | aspect, side |
| poristhiti | পরিস্থিতি | situation |
| ghotona | ঘটনা | incident |
| prokriya | প্রক্রিয়া | process |
| manodondo | মানদণ্ড | standard, criterion |
| subidha / osubidha | সুবিধা / অসুবিধা | pro / con |
| gurutto | গুরুত্ব | importance |
| dharona | ধারণা | notion, idea |
| uddeshyo | উদ্দেশ্য | purpose |

## Which word?

**folafol vs porinoti.** folafol is a neutral result: an exam result, the outcome of a vote. porinoti is where something ends up, and it usually sounds like a warning.

**poristhiti vs obostha.** poristhiti is the situation around you (desh-er poristhiti). obostha is the state of a person or thing (or shorir-er obostha = his health).

**mulyo vs dam.** dam is the price you pay at the shop. mulyo is worth in the abstract (somoyer mulyo). In formal writing it also means price.

**ortho vs tatporjo.** ortho is what a word or sentence means. tatporjo is why something matters.

**parthokko vs tofat.** Same meaning. tofat is more casual.

## Examples

- emon sujog bar bar ashe na, chhede dio na: Chances like this don't come often, don't let it go
- or kotha-r probhab sobar opor porechhe: What she said affected everyone
- ek-ta shorte raji hote pari: I can agree on one condition
- poristhiti ekhon onek-ta niyontrone: The situation is a lot more under control now
- mul bishoy-e asho, eto ghuriye bolchho keno?: Get to the point, why are you going around in circles?
- ei chakri-r subidha holo bari theke kaj kora jay: The upside of this job is you can work from home
- tumi or kotha-ke eto gurutto dichho keno?: Why are you taking what he says so seriously?
- share bazar niye amar kono dharona nei: I have no idea about the stock market
- prosongo bodlo na, age amar proshno-r uttor dao: Don't change the subject, answer my question first
- mithye bolar porinoti kintu bhalo hoy na: Lying never ends well, you know

cards.Example: emon sujog bar bar ashe na: An opportunity like this doesn't come often
cards.Notes: sujog newa = take the chance, also 'take advantage of someone' (amar sujog niyechhe).

cards.Example: or kotha-r probhab chhelemeye-der opor onek: Her words have a big influence on the kids
cards.Notes: probhab fela = to have an effect on (opor probhab fela); prabhabshali = influential.

cards.English: condition (a term, as in 'on one condition')
cards.Example: ek-ta shorte raji achhi, tumi-o ashbe: I'll agree on one condition, you come too
cards.Notes: Not for health or the state of something (that's obostha). shorto-sapekkhe = subject to conditions.

cards.Example: eto khatar por-o folafol bhalo holo na: Even after all that work the result wasn't good
cards.Notes: Also exam results. In speech result is common; fol (fruit) alone also means result in fixed phrases (er fol).

cards.Example: deri-r karon-ta ki?: What's the reason for the delay?
cards.Notes: Also used as 'because' at the start of a clause; ki karone = for what reason (formal).

cards.Example: somoy-er mulyo bujhte shekho: Learn to understand the value of time
cards.Notes: dam is the everyday word for price; mulyo is abstract worth, or price in formal writing (mulyobriddhi = price rise).

cards.Example: eto boro kaj korar khomota amader nei: We don't have the capacity to do such a big job
cards.Notes: Also political power (khomotay asha = come to power). khomotabaan = powerful.

cards.Example: ei rayer tatporjo onek: This verdict is very significant
cards.Notes: Educated register; ortho is plain meaning, tatporjo is why something matters. tatporjopurno = significant.

cards.Example: byapar-ta-r arek-ta dik-o bhebe dekho: Think about the other side of the matter too
cards.Notes: Same word as direction. bhalo dik / kharap dik = upside / downside.

cards.Example: poristhiti bujhe byabostha nebo: I'll act depending on the situation
cards.Notes: obostha is someone's or something's state; poristhiti is the wider situation around you.

cards.Example: kal raste ek-ta odbhut ghotona ghotlo: A strange thing happened on the road yesterday
cards.Notes: ghotona ghota = an event happens. For a planned event (party, function) say anushthan or program.

cards.Example: visa pawar prokriya-ta khub lomba: The visa process is very long
cards.Notes: Spoken often just process; prokriya is standard in formal talk and news.

cards.Example: mul bishoy-e asho, ghuriye bolo na: Get to the main point, don't beat around the bush
cards.Notes: mul kotha is the more casual version (mul kotha-ta holo... = the main thing is...).

cards.Example: kon manodonde tumi eta bhalo bolchho?: By what standard are you calling this good?
cards.Notes: Formal; in speech people also say standard. man alone = quality level (kajer man bhalo).

cards.Example: ei flat-er subidha holo station-ta kachhe: The advantage of this flat is the station is close
cards.Notes: Also facility (hospital-e sob subidha achhe). subidha-osubidha = pros and cons.

cards.Example: ekmatro osubidha holo bhara-ta beshi: The only downside is the rent is high
cards.Notes: Also polite 'trouble': kono osubidha hole bolo = tell me if anything's a problem.

cards.Example: or kotha-r kono gurutto nei: What he says doesn't matter
cards.Notes: gurutopurno = important (formal); in speech important or joruri is common.

cards.English: to give importance to / take seriously
cards.Example: boss amar proposal-ke gurutto dilen na: The boss didn't take my proposal seriously
cards.Notes: Negative is common: gurutto dao na = don't take it seriously.

cards.Example: ei meeting-er uddeshyo-ta ki?: What's the purpose of this meeting?
cards.Notes: kono uddeshyo chhara = for no reason / aimlessly. lokkho is a target or goal.

cards.Example: prosongo bodlo na, age eta-r uttor dao: Don't change the subject, answer this first
cards.Notes: prosongo bodlano = change the subject; prasongik = relevant.

cards.Example: ei project-e tomar bhumika ki chhilo?: What was your role in this project?
cards.Notes: Also a film role and a book's preface. bhumika palon kora = play a role.

cards.Example: aaj brishti hobar sombhabona achhe: There's a chance of rain today
cards.Notes: Also potential: chhele-tar sombhabona achhe = the boy has potential.

cards.Example: protyek-ta system-er kichhu simabaddhota thake: Every system has some limitations
cards.Notes: Educated register; sima = limit, simito = limited.

cards.Example: eto mithye bolar porinoti bhalo hobe na: Telling so many lies won't end well
cards.Notes: folafol is a neutral result; porinoti is where something ends up, often a warning.

cards.Example: dutor modhye parthokko-ta ki?: What's the difference between the two?
cards.Notes: tofat is the casual synonym (onek tofat = big difference).

cards.Example: ei niyom-er kono byatikrom nei: There's no exception to this rule
cards.Notes: Also an unusual person: o ekdom byatikrom = she's one of a kind.

cards.Example: sob-ta tomar sidhanter opor nirbhor korchhe: Everything depends on your decision
cards.Notes: Takes opor (on). Also 'rely on a person': ami or opor nirbhor kori.
A natural way to avoid a yes/no; shorter: poristhiti-r opor.
Casual alternative: seta onno kotha (that's a different matter).
